skill.name: wunderui-token-check
skill.description: Find hardcoded colors, spacing, and radii in WunderUI projects and compare them with bundled design tokens. Review measured differences before applying supported replacements.
skill.summary: Compare hardcoded styles with WunderUI tokens and apply reviewed replacements with measured differences.
skill.author: wunder-ui

security_audit.summary: Most static findings match harmless regular expressions, template strings, documentation, or expected local operations. Four findings confirm unsafe report output or report-supplied paths, allowing external file overwrites through symlinks or a tampered report. A separate semantic finding identifies symlink traversal during scanning; no evidence found of malicious intent, prompt injection, credential collection, or network transmission.

remediation.issue: Fix accepts report-supplied paths and replacements without validating their origin or project boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the report schema and regenerate approved findings from current source. Resolve real paths, reject traversal outside approved roots, and verify source hashes before writing.

remediation.issue: Scan writes its report through existing symlinks without validating the output target.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinked report directories and files, enforce realpath containment, and use exclusive creation or a securely created temporary file before atomic replacement.

remediation.issue: Directory traversal follows symlinks without checking scan boundaries or tracking visited directories.
remediation.suggestion: Use lstat to reject symlinks by default. If links are explicitly allowed, enforce realpath containment and track visited directories to prevent cycles.

semantic_findings.description: The scanner follows symlinks with statSync and recurses without realpath containment or cycle detection. A repository link can expose external source literals in reports or cause recursive resource exhaustion.

content.user_title: Replace Hardcoded Styles with WunderUI Tokens
content.value_statement: Hardcoded colors and dimensions make WunderUI projects harder to theme consistently. This skill compares literals with bundled tokens and supports reviewed replacements with measured differences.
actual_capabilities: Find color, pixel-spacing, and radius literals in supported source files, including arbitrary Tailwind classes and selected CSS declarations.
Rank three nearby color tokens using OKLab distance, semantic roles, and bundled light and dark values.
Compare spacing with the documented spacing scale and radii with bundled radius tokens.
Classify findings as swap, visible, or review using measured color or pixel differences.
Apply supported color and radius replacements and arbitrary Tailwind spacing replacements, with optional identifier and alternative selection.
Save a local findings report and print counts, applied changes, and maximum measured shifts.
limitations: Requires Node.js 20 or later and uses a bundled token snapshot, not live project theme discovery.
Line-based regular expressions cannot fully understand syntax, runtime styles, transparency, accessibility, or visual equivalence.
CSS spacing declarations and several inline dimension forms require manual edits; motion tokens are not audited.
Fix trusts report paths, and scanning follows symlinks; use trusted reports and inspect project links before execution.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Component Styles
use_cases.description: Compare component literals with WunderUI tokens and review supported replacements before editing source.

use_cases.title: Review Token Coverage
use_cases.description: Group distant values and decide whether each needs an existing semantic token, a new token, or an explicit exception.

use_cases.title: Prepare Theme Changes
use_cases.description: Inspect fixed colors and suggested light and dark values before planning a theming migration.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Without Editing
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my trusted WunderUI project for hardcoded colors, spacing, and radii. Inspect symlinks before scanning. Summarize findings without changing source files.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this component and explain its nearest tokens and measured differences. Compare suggested light and dark values. Do not apply replacements until I approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: evaluate a focused token migration.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Approved Matches
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a fresh report for these trusted source folders. Show the proposed swap replacements and wait for approval. Then apply them, rescan, and run project checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: perform controlled replacement and verification.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Theme Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Group review findings by value and semantic role. Recommend mappings or exceptions, including dark-mode effects. Propose explicit selections for approval and identify manual spacing edits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate design decisions across components.

output_examples.input: Inspect a component with arbitrary padding of 16 pixels and a radius of 10 pixels.
output: Padding: the spacing scale has an exact 16-pixel match, classified as swap.
Radius: the nearest bundled radius is 8 pixels, a 2-pixel difference classified as visible.

output_examples.input: Inspect a fixed white background before adding dark mode.
output: Fixed white background: classified as visible because replacing it with a semantic token changes dark-mode behavior.
The bundled background token is white in light mode and dark in dark mode.
Review the intended surface role before approving a replacement.

best_practices: Use a clean version-control checkpoint, trusted source folders, and a freshly generated report; inspect symlinks and report targets before fixing.
Approve replacements by semantic role and inspect both theme modes rather than relying only on measured distance.
Rescan after edits, review the diff, run project checks, and inspect affected components visually.
anti_patterns: Running fix against a supplied or tampered report without checking its paths and replacements.
Treating low color distance as proof of accessibility, transparency preservation, or identical dark-mode behavior.
Replacing every review finding automatically or changing artwork and brand colors without a design decision.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running the bundled scanner requires an environment that can execute local Node.js commands.

faq.question: What must my project provide?
faq.answer: Use Node.js 20 or later and a WunderUI project with the corresponding tokens available. The script has no package dependencies.

faq.question: What do swap, visible, and review mean?
faq.answer: Swap means color distance at most 2 or an exact dimension match. Visible allows distance at most 6 or 2 pixels. Review needs a design decision.

faq.question: Does it rewrite every finding?
faq.answer: No. Default fix selects swap findings; visible findings require an option. CSS spacing declarations and unsupported inline dimensions need manual edits.

faq.question: Does it send project data to a service?
faq.answer: No network transmission was found in the reviewed files. The script reads local source and writes a local report.

faq.question: What security precautions are necessary?
faq.answer: Fix does not validate report paths, and scanning follows symlinks. Use trusted projects, regenerate reports, inspect targets, and keep recoverable source changes.
